keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance from the closest point of the Earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle may request authorisation to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

Registration in Italy via the D-Flight portal (except for the exemptions listed below): Basic subscription €7/year (PRO €28/year) + mandatory QR code on each drone (Base €7/UAS; the first one is included with the initial subscription)
Exempt: toy drones (Directive 2009/48/EC) do not require registration, a certificate or insurance; drones under 250 g without a camera or microphone do not require registration.

Foreign pilots: operator registration is valid in all EU countries and in Switzerland. If you are already registered in your own EU country, you do not need to register on D-Flight: just display your operator number on the drone. Residents outside the EU (including the United Kingdom) register in the first EU country they intend to visit.

In Italy, the minimum age to fly in A1/A3 is 16; minors (aged 16-17) need the consent of a parent or legal guardian to register on the ENAC portal. The online certificate (40 questions) is valid for 5 years.

Third-party liability insurance is mandatory for all drones (including under 250 g and for recreational use), except toy drones (Dir. 2009/48/EC) — minimum coverage 750,000 SDR, under Art. 27 of the Regolamento UAS-IT and Art. 1015 of the Codice della Navigazione.
Rome and Vatican City: Extensive No-Fly Zones

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your direct visual line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication between you at all times so that you can jointly monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. "Follow-me" mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official table.

There is no single distance from airports: aerodrome geographical zones (ENAC Circular ATM-09A) are published on D-Flight. In the open category, flying is prohibited inside these zones, which start at a different height depending on their colour (red 0 m, orange 25 m, yellow 45 m); in the rest of ATZs and CTRs the zone normally starts at 60 m. Below these heights you may fly without an airspace reservation; to fly inside the zones you need the specific category with clearance from ENAC or the Aeronautica Militare.

Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline, provided that the required green flashing light is used, unless a national rule or a rule for a specific geographical zone imposes stricter conditions.
Historic sites and archaeological areas may be subject to additional restrictions
Nature parks: flying over them is prohibited where the ENAC-approved ban is published on D-Flight; to fly there you need clearance from the park authority (Ente Parco).
Drones with a C1, C2 or C3 class mark: direct remote identification and geo-awareness must be active and up to date.
importantNotes: D-Flight subscription: Basic €7/year (PRO €28/year for the Specific Category). The first Base QR Code is included with initial activation; additional Base QR Codes cost €7 per UAS (PRO €112 per UAS).
Mandatory insurance with a minimum coverage of 750,000 SDRs (Special Drawing Rights)

Rome: the city centre is a no-fly zone for security reasons, where overflight is prohibited for all aircraft, including drones; any exemptions also require clearance from the Prefettura di Roma. Always check D-Flight.
Fines of up to 100,000 € for serious violations
The GDPR applies when identifiable images are captured
